change.title: Create IBM Project Chess and competitive response to Logix
change.reason: Create the requested IBM Project Chess/reaction envelope. event.ibm_investigate is period.start; the four requested steps retain their dates in chronological order. Leave period.end unknown rather than treating the March 1982 forecast as a completed release.

after.title: IBM Project Chess and competitive response to Logix
after.description: Starting with the confidential personal-computer market investigation on 5 July 1979, IBM responds to the business-computing market developed by Logix, Tandy, Apple and independent software suppliers. Project authorisation leads to software sourcing review, funding of an alternative OS programme and business-software qualification. The recorded qualification delays do not establish a completed IBM release.

participant.role: market investigation, PC project sponsor and software qualification lead

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch establishes the competing business-computing platform and workflows IBM subsequently benchmarks.
Assess competing applications, interfaces, distribution, training, service and independent OS suppliers before committing the project’s delivery approach.

steps.description: Authorise IBM’s personal-computer project in response to independent suppliers’ business applications and channels.
Review software sourcing and identify the gap between available OS options and the required schedule.
Fund an alternative OS delivery programme and stabilise application interfaces while hardware development continues.
Record OS integration, application qualification and support delays; keep the projected commercial release distinct from a confirmed launch.

outcomes.description: IBM has authorised its PC project, identified a software sourcing gap and funded substitute OS work. Software integration, applications and service qualification determine commercial timing; supplier identity, OS name and a confirmed release remain unresolved.

change.title: Revise Apple business-market response to Logix and AION
change.reason: Add the Apple–Peachtree package as a step. Extend the calendar end to 15 March 1980 and move the former closing compatibility review into steps, preserving one placement per event and the explicit request that apple_business is a step.

before.title: Apple business-market response to Logix and AION
before.description: Apple responds to Aurelia and AION business software through software recruitment, selective dealer demonstrations, partner searches, Peachtree cooperation and complete-system promotions. The recorded response runs from July 1978 through the September 1979 review of successor-product compatibility requirements; it does not imply a guaranteed technical fix or an accelerated Lisa/GUI release.

participant.role: organiser of the competitive business-software and dealer response

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch and its integrated business-software demonstrations prompt Apple to strengthen its own software partnerships and business-dealer offering.

steps.description: Prepare selective business-dealer demonstrations, complete-system quotations and introductory customer lessons.
Expand the business-software initiative into searches and negotiations for independent accounting, spreadsheet and database partners.
Pursue the recorded Apple–Peachtree accounting cooperation while continuing separate spreadsheet and database efforts; retain the agreement’s existing negotiation status.
Promote complete Apple II business configurations, demonstrations and introductory lessons.

outcomes.description: Apple has organised a coordinated response encompassing business-software recruitment, selective dealer demonstrations, Peachtree accounting cooperation and complete-configuration promotions. These activities establish no guaranteed sales, finished spring-1979 package or nationwide training network.
Apple has reviewed compatibility requirements for successor products, prioritising protection of existing software, peripherals and customer data while retaining its independent hardware roadmap.

change.title: Revise Aurelia standards and third-party ecosystem development
change.reason: Extend the ecosystem envelope to 31 March 1980 so it still contains the expanded Tandy cooperation child; preserve all other memberships and dates.

before.title: Aurelia standards and third-party ecosystem development
before.description: Build the initial ecosystem of independent manufacturers, software developers and peripheral contributors around Aurelia’s CP/M with TUI, FlexiBUS, C development interfaces, graphics subsystem and digital monitor connectivity. Coordinate documented implementation and qualification, SMC second-source transfer, portable DRI extensions and Tandy cooperation. The envelope covers the recorded July 1978 to October 1979 work; it does not imply universal adoption or completion of all later ecosystem targets.

participant.role: C development platform and application integration

inputs.description: Aurelia’s launch provides the working software, peripheral and display platform for independent implementations and supplier cooperation.
Use documented software APIs, bus rules, graphics profiles and monitor-link specifications, with explicit licensing and host-specific qualification.

outcomes.description: Independent contributors have a documented implementation and qualification programme covering CP/M/TUI, FlexiBUS, C development, graphics APIs and monitor connectivity. Final access terms and unverified participation remain subject to the existing agreements and qualification requirements.

The recorded milestones include portable DRI extension release, the supported Tandy configuration and initial qualified SMC chip sales. They do not establish release of every licensed chip or universal compatibility.
Microsoft BASIC has a recorded Aurelia release as independently licensed third-party software.

steps.description: Transfer engineering knowledge and qualify independently manufactured SMC chips.

Document CP/M/TUI services, FlexiBUS device interfaces, the C development platform and graphics/display APIs. Provide reference integrations and conformance guidance; distinguish software API support from optional display hardware and qualified monitor connectivity.
Implement and qualify Tandy’s supported Model II CP/M, Abacus and FlexiBUS option without requiring Logix video hardware.
Begin external OEM implementations, documentation and qualification of portable CP/M extensions.
Release documented optional TUI, capability-discovery and FlexiBUS extensions for non-Logix manufacturers.
Microsoft releases licensed Microsoft BASIC for Aurelia at NCC 1979, contributing third-party language software to the ecosystem.

change.title: Revise Stepper procurement, installation and process development
change.reason: Nest DRAM yield-control and repair work and add the four manufacturing milestones as direct steps. Preserve their month-level dates, maturity transitions and qualification limits; the existing December 1982 end already contains them.

before.title: Stepper procurement, installation and process development
before.description: From the January 1979 stepper order, procure and install the lithography equipment, record installation acceptance in September 1979, and coordinate 2.75 µm and 2.0 µm process and memory qualification through December 1982. Installation acceptance does not by itself qualify every process or product; existing processors retain their specified process until separately qualified.

inputs.description: The starting order authorises procurement; process development must meet measured tool-matching, retention, speed, yield and release gates rather than treating installation as production qualification.

outcomes.description: The programme records stepper installation acceptance and encompasses the two process-development and memory-qualification workstreams through their stated endpoints. Capability and part availability remain governed by their individual qualification records.

steps.description: Develop and qualify the dated manufacturing scenario; ERA1 remains on 3 µm. Budgets, yields and release gates are in memory_manufacturing.json.
Develop and qualify the 2.75 µm process and memory capabilities from July 1979 through June 1981.
Record stepper installation and lithography acceptance in September 1979, retaining month precision.
Develop the 2.0 µm process and RAM shrinks from January 1981 through December 1982.

after.title: Stepper procurement, installation and process development
after.description: From the January 1979 stepper order, procure and install the lithography equipment, record installation acceptance in September 1979, and coordinate DRAM yield-control and repair work plus 2.75 µm and 2.0 µm process and memory qualification through December 1982. Installation acceptance does not by itself qualify every process or product; existing processors retain their specified process until separately qualified.

inputs.description: The starting order authorises procurement; process development must meet measured tool-matching, retention, speed, yield and release gates rather than treating installation as production qualification.

outcomes.description: The programme records stepper acceptance, DRAM control and repair development, and the 2.75 µm and 2.0 µm qualification workstreams and release milestones. Individual capability transitions and part availability remain governed by their qualification records.

steps.description: Develop and qualify the dated manufacturing scenario; ERA1 remains on 3 µm. Budgets, yields and release gates are in memory_manufacturing.json.

Develop DRAM yield control and repair during the recorded 1980 workstream.
Record the improved 3 µm DRAM process-control release in June 1980, retaining its existing capability transition.
Record the selected 2.75 µm process release review in June 1980, subject to its existing measured qualification requirements.
Develop the 2.0 µm process and RAM shrinks from January 1981 through December 1982.
Record the first complete 2.0 µm pilot lots in September 1981.
Record the selected 2.0 µm production release review in June 1982.
